label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article II, Section 3. The President gives Congress information of the state of the Union and recommends measures to it; on extraordinary occasions he may convene both houses or either of them, and if they disagree about the time of adjournment he may adjourn them to such time as he thinks proper; he receives ambassadors and other public ministers, takes care that the laws be faithfully executed, and commissions all the officers of the United States.
This story is about the executive bringing criminal charges under laws already on the books.

On April 22, 1793 Washington proclaimed that the United States would pursue a conduct "friendly and impartial toward the belligerant Powers," and said he had given instructions to officers "to cause prosecutions to be instituted against all persons" who violate the law of nations within the cognizance of the courts of the United States.
D'iu is charged with stalking employees and possessing falsified identity documents.
Handlers directed D'iu to collect facts about the company.
D'iu has been held in jail since 2 November.

The strongest argument against this is that charging and holding this man stretches this duty beyond faithful execution of existing law into a foreign-policy statement about another country's war, and that the executive should not treat ordinary criminal process as a tool to answer overseas conflict.
We read this clause to mean the executive must carry out laws that already exist.
Conspiracy and collusion can be imputable under those laws by ordinary charges.
This keeps the carrying-out power with the branch set up for it.
